questions.question: Which statement describes a typical characteristic of a project?

options.A: Projects are unlimited in time and use few capacity resources
options.B: Projects involve one department and have no quality demands
options.C: Projects are usually complex and unique and involve a high degree of risk
options.D: Projects are routine tasks with standardized, repeatable results

questions.explanation: Projects are also limited in duration, cost and capacity intensive, involve several departments and are of strategic significance.

questions.question: How is a project defined in the course?

options.A: An undertaking whose general conditions and constraints are unique to it
options.B: A recurring activity that is repeated every fiscal period
options.C: A set of master data records used by several departments
options.D: A budget approved by management for one fiscal year

questions.explanation: General conditions: the objectives, the time frame, and the financial and capacity-related restrictions.

questions.question: Which are the general conditions of a project?

options.A: The profit centers, the plants, and the company codes involved
options.B: The vendors, the customers, and the bank accounts involved
options.C: The objectives, the time frame, and the financial and capacity-related restrictions
options.D: The cost elements, the activity types, and the settlement rules

questions.explanation: These conditions make every project unique.

questions.question: Why are project structures arranged as a hierarchy?

options.A: To keep every activity independent from the other project objects
options.B: To evaluate aggregated data, allocate budgets and define responsibilities
options.C: To replace the need for planning dates, resources and costs
options.D: To limit each project to exactly one organizational unit

questions.explanation: The hierarchy lets dates, resources, costs, budgets and payments be planned, controlled and monitored transparently.

questions.question: Between which parties are the precise targets of a project agreed?

options.A: The vendor and the plant manager
options.B: The controller and the cost center owner
options.C: The auditor and the project team member
options.D: The contractor and the sold-to party

questions.explanation: Projects have precise targets agreed on between the contractor and the sold-to party.

questions.question: Which of the following can be a project, according to the course?

options.A: Only construction projects in the building industry
options.B: Research and development, investment measures, make-to-order production, or extensive maintenance tasks
options.C: Only routine production orders for stock items
options.D: Only software implementation projects of a company

questions.explanation: The term project is not specific to a particular industry sector.

questions.question: For which kinds of projects is the planned finish date of major relevance, and for which are budgeted costs more important?

options.A: Finish date: investment projects; budgeted costs: customer projects
options.B: Finish date and costs: only for customer projects
options.C: Neither aspect depends on the type of the project
options.D: Finish date: customer projects; budgeted costs: investment projects

questions.explanation: The aspects of planning are mutually dependent: more resources keep a deadline but increase costs.

questions.question: Which two structures does SAP PS provide for mapping projects?

options.A: Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) and network
options.B: Profit center hierarchy and cost center hierarchy
options.C: Bill of materials and routing
options.D: Project definition and budget profile

questions.explanation: The WBS shows activities hierarchically; networks show the flow of the project.

questions.question: What is a work breakdown structure (WBS)?

options.A: A diagram of activities linked by their temporal and logical relationships
options.B: A list of document info records assigned to the activities
options.C: A model of a project showing the required activities in a hierarchical form, the basis for planning costs, revenues, payments, scheduling and budgeting
options.D: A set of settlement rules that allocate the costs of the project

questions.explanation: The various work packages are described as individual WBS elements.

questions.question: What does a network represent in SAP PS?

options.A: The individual project activities with their temporal and logical relationships (the flow of the project)
options.B: The hierarchical breakdown of the project into work packages
options.C: The budget assigned to each work package of the project
options.D: The organizational units assigned to each project element

questions.explanation: Networks link the activities and define in what chronological order they are performed.

questions.question: What do activities form in a project?

options.A: The hierarchical basis for assigning organizational units
options.B: The legal basis for the contract with the sold-to party
options.C: The financial basis for approving the project budget
options.D: The operative basis for planning and controlling dates, costs and resources

questions.explanation: Activities are linked by relationships and can be grouped into networks.

questions.question: What happens when activities are assigned to WBS elements?

options.A: The WBS elements become billing elements automatically
options.B: The dates and costs of the activities are aggregated at the WBS level and can be evaluated there
options.C: The activities are removed from the network structure
options.D: The budget of the WBS elements is released for posting

questions.explanation: Activity funds already assigned are checked against the budgets of the WBS elements.

questions.question: What is the project definition?

options.A: The lowest level WBS element in which actual costs are posted
options.B: The list of activities and relationships in the network
options.C: The set of settlement rules for the project at period end
options.D: The framework for all objects of a project, containing data that affects the whole project and default values for WBS elements

questions.explanation: It contains start and finish dates, organizational data and planning parameters.

questions.question: For which project data is the controlling area specified only once?

options.A: Each WBS element; every element can have its own controlling area
options.B: The project definition; it is unique for the entire project
options.C: Each activity; every activity uses a different controlling area
options.D: Each network; every network is assigned to a different area

questions.explanation: The controlling area is specified when the project definition is created.

questions.question: Which of the following can be done with WBS elements?

options.A: Plan costs and revenues, post actual costs, enter a budget, assign purchase requisitions and plan payments
options.B: Plan only dates; costs and budgets are handled in the network
options.C: Post goods receipts but not vendor invoices to the project
options.D: Define activity types and capacity requirements of work centers

questions.explanation: WBS elements also allow dates to be planned manually.

questions.question: Why can projects be processed across companies?

options.A: The project definition is assigned to several company codes at once
options.B: All WBS elements of a project must belong to the same controlling area
options.C: Each WBS element is assigned its own company code, so different WBS elements can use different company codes
options.D: The network header contains the company codes of all the activities

questions.explanation: Organizational units such as profit centers and business areas can also be assigned to each WBS element.

questions.question: Which of the following can be assigned to WBS elements for reporting?

options.A: Plants, storage locations and purchasing groups responsible for the project
options.B: Profit centers, business areas, persons responsible, partners and cost centers responsible for the project
options.C: Sales areas, distribution channels and divisions responsible for the project
options.D: Company codes only, because other assignments are not permitted

questions.explanation: These assignments are used mainly for reporting and project summarization.

questions.question: What is the Project Builder?

options.A: A report that compares planned and actual project progress values
options.B: A budget profile for assigning funds to the project and its parts
options.C: A transaction that settles the costs of a project to receivers
options.D: A user-friendly tool in SAP PS for creating and editing projects quickly, covering all objects except PRT assignment

questions.explanation: It offers context-sensitive menus, drag and relate, a worklist and templates.

questions.question: The Project Builder window is divided into which three areas?

options.A: Header data, object list and cost view
options.B: Structure overview, worklist and work area
options.C: Planning board, budget view and settlement view
options.D: Project definition, WBS overview and network overview

questions.explanation: The worklist stores frequently used projects, networks and WBS elements per user.

questions.question: Which objects can be used as templates when creating a project?

options.A: Only the budgets of projects that were already settled
options.B: Only the notifications of the maintenance plant
options.C: Only the cost center groups of the controlling area
options.D: Operative projects and standard projects, including standard WBSs and standard networks

questions.explanation: Projects can be copied with all lower-level objects: WBS elements, activities, texts, documents, milestones and components.

questions.question: Which operative indicator marks WBS elements for which costs are planned manually?

options.A: Account assignment element
options.B: Planning element
options.C: Billing element
options.D: Statistic indicator

questions.explanation: Operative indicators define the characteristics of a WBS element.

questions.question: Which operative indicator marks WBS elements to which actual costs are posted?

options.A: Planning element
options.B: Billing element
options.C: Statistic indicator
options.D: Account assignment element

questions.explanation: Actual costs can only be posted to account assignment elements.

questions.question: Which operative indicator marks WBS elements to which revenues are posted?

options.A: Planning element
options.B: Billing element
options.C: Account assignment element
options.D: Statistic indicator

questions.explanation: Results analysis is usually performed in the billing element.

questions.question: What does the Statistic indicator of a WBS element specify?

options.A: Whether the element may be used to plan costs manually
options.B: Whether the element is allowed to receive revenue postings
options.C: Whether the element is used only for statistical purposes or works with real costs
options.D: Whether the element belongs to the standard project template

questions.explanation: A statistical WBS element does not carry real costs.

questions.question: In the example, planning is carried out as far as level 2 of the hierarchy. What does that mean for level 3 WBS elements?

options.A: They are not planning elements
options.B: They are planning elements
options.C: They are billing elements
options.D: They are statistical WBS elements

questions.explanation: Only elements flagged as planning elements can be used for manual cost planning.

questions.question: What does a network header contain?

options.A: The planned costs of every activity in the network
options.B: The WBS elements that are billing elements
options.C: Control data and default values for the entire network
options.D: The budget profile and the budget release dates

questions.explanation: Each network has exactly one header.

questions.question: For what are milestones assigned to activities and WBS elements used?

options.A: To document important events, for milestone billing in SD, and to start automatic workflow tasks
options.B: To post actual costs and revenues to the activities
options.C: To release the budget in various points of the fiscal year
options.D: To assign production resources and tools to the activities

questions.explanation: Dates of milestones can be referenced in billing or invoicing plans.

questions.question: Networks form the basis for planning which quantity structures?

options.A: Budgets, supplements, returns and transfers of funds
options.B: Dates (scheduling), costs (costing), resources and material requirements
options.C: Cost centers, profit centers, plants and company codes
options.D: Settlement rules, overhead rates and interest calculation

questions.explanation: Dates and costs arise automatically via scheduling and costing.

questions.question: Which activity categories does SAP PS have?

options.A: Planning, budgeting, execution and settlement
options.B: Notification, planning, control and completion
options.C: Stock, non-stock, text and document activities
options.D: Internal processing, external processing, services and cost activities

questions.explanation: Cost activities plan additional primary costs.

questions.question: What are project structure texts?

options.A: Original documents in Word or CAD formats stored in the DMS
options.B: User-definable texts managed in a text catalog and classified into text types, assignable to WBS elements or activities
options.C: Notes created automatically when the budget is exceeded
options.D: Master data of the partners assigned to the WBS elements

questions.explanation: Document info records via SAP DMS handle original documents such as Excel, Word, PPT and CAD files.

questions.question: Which aspects can be planned in a project system?

options.A: Resources, dates, materials, revenue, costs, payments and project structures
options.B: Only the dates and costs of the project
options.C: Only the resources and the materials of the project
options.D: Only the budget and the settlement of the project

questions.explanation: Which aspect is prioritized depends on the type of project.

questions.question: What is an internally processed activity used for?

options.A: To procure services that are provided by other companies
options.B: To plan additional primary costs without capacity requirements
options.C: To plan work carried out within the company, determining the output of machines or personnel
options.D: To assign milestones to the project for billing purposes

questions.explanation: It requires a work center, work, duration and activity type so capacity requirements and costs can be calculated.

questions.question: Which data must be defined for an internally processed activity so that capacity requirements and costs can be calculated?

options.A: Work center, work, duration and activity type
options.B: Vendor, purchasing group, plant and storage location
options.C: Budget profile, user status, supplement and transfer
options.D: Settlement rule, overhead rate, interest and forecast

questions.explanation: The work center contains scheduling, capacity and costing data.

questions.question: What is "work" in an internally processed activity?

options.A: The length of time for which the activity lasts
options.B: The place where the activity is carried out
options.C: The price used to calculate the planned costs
options.D: The planned output of machines or personnel needed to complete the activity

questions.explanation: Duration specifies how long an activity lasts.

questions.question: What do the activity type and the cost center derived from the work center specify?

options.A: The duration of the activity in working days
options.B: A price for calculating the planned costs of an activity
options.C: The capacity requirements of the activity
options.D: The budget available for the activity

questions.explanation: This is how planned internal activity costs are calculated.

questions.question: What is an externally processed activity?

options.A: An activity carried out by workers of the company in its own work centers
options.B: An activity used only to plan additional primary costs in the network
options.C: An activity for which a goods receipt is always posted to stock
options.D: An activity that specifies services to be provided by other companies, processed through purchasing

questions.explanation: Example: commissioning an engineering office to design a machine.

questions.question: What is automatically created when an externally processed activity is created?

options.A: A production order that is released automatically
options.B: A purchase requisition that is processed further in purchasing
options.C: A maintenance order for the work center
options.D: A service entry sheet for the activity

questions.explanation: Data from a purchasing info record (prices, delivery times) can be used.

questions.question: How does a service activity differ from an externally processed activity?

options.A: A service activity allows service specifications and value limits for unplanned services; services are entered via a service entry sheet instead of a goods receipt
options.B: A service activity is processed in the company; an external one is not
options.C: A service activity needs a goods receipt; an external activity does not
options.D: A service activity creates a production order for the service

questions.explanation: The service purchasing process involves two steps: entry of the service and acceptance of the service.

questions.question: Which tool can be used to level the capacities of work centers during project planning?

options.A: The Project Builder worklist
options.B: The budget release function
options.C: The Project Planning Board
options.D: The settlement rule transaction

questions.explanation: It helps decide how much of a work center's capacity is used by the activities.

questions.question: How does a project budget differ from the project cost plan?

options.A: The budget is only an estimate and can be ignored during execution
options.B: The budget is binding and approved by management as the anticipated development of costs
options.C: The budget contains revenues while the cost plan contains payments
options.D: The budget is created before the WBS is defined for the project

questions.explanation: Cost planning estimates costs as accurately as possible; funds are assigned as budget in the approval phase.

questions.question: Which function assigns funds to a project and its components?

options.A: Budget carry forward
options.B: Budget release
options.C: Progress analysis
options.D: Maintain original budget

questions.explanation: The budget profile determines whether funds are lump values or distributed by year.

questions.question: What does the budget profile specify?

options.A: Which WBS elements are billing elements in the project
options.B: Whether funds are assigned as lump values or distributed by year
options.C: Which activities are internally or externally processed
options.D: Which receivers are allowed in the settlement rule

questions.explanation: It is used with the maintain original budget function.

questions.question: How can the original budget be changed after it has been frozen with a user status?

options.A: By overwriting the original budget amount directly
options.B: By deleting the WBS elements and creating them again
options.C: Only by defining supplements, returns and transfers
options.D: By releasing the project to the next fiscal year

questions.explanation: A user status can prevent users from maintaining the overall project budget.

questions.question: What does the budget release function do?

options.A: Makes funds available at various points within a fiscal year
options.B: Transfers unused funds to the budget of the new fiscal year
options.C: Approves the project cost plan for the next period
options.D: Locks the original budget for all users

questions.explanation: Budget carry forward transfers funds not used in the previous year.

questions.question: What does the budget carry forward function do?

options.A: Makes funds available at various points within the fiscal year
options.B: Increases the original budget by a supplement
options.C: Transfers funds not used in the previous year to the budget of the new fiscal year
options.D: Settles the unused funds to a cost center

questions.explanation: It is the counterpart of the budget release function.

questions.question: What do material components establish in SAP PS?

options.A: A link between PS and Sales and Distribution, Materials Management and Production Planning
options.B: A link between PS and Human Capital Management and Asset Accounting
options.C: A link between PS and Warehouse Management and Transportation
options.D: A link between PS and Controlling and Financial Accounting only

questions.explanation: Material requirements in projects form the basis for procurement.

questions.question: Which item category is used for materials kept in warehouse, project or sales order stock?

options.A: Non-stock item (category N)
options.B: Stock item
options.C: Service item
options.D: Text item

questions.explanation: Reservations are created for stock items.

questions.question: How is a non-stock item (item category N) procured?

options.A: Through the warehouse, with a reservation for the goods in stock
options.B: Through the production order that is converted from a planned order
options.C: Through a transfer posting from the project stock to the activity
options.D: Directly by the network activity: a purchase requisition is created and the goods are posted to the activity, not to stock

questions.explanation: Non-stock items cannot be managed as project stock or sales order stock.

questions.question: Which procurement element does requirements planning create for in-house production and for external procurement?

options.A: A production order for in-house; a purchase order for external
options.B: A planned order for in-house production; a purchase requisition for external procurement
options.C: A purchase requisition for in-house; a planned order for external
options.D: A sales order for in-house; a delivery for external

questions.explanation: Planned elements are then converted into production orders and purchase orders.

questions.question: What is the purpose of period-end closing in a project?

options.A: To create the project definition and WBS for the next period
options.B: To assign a budget profile to the WBS elements of the project
options.C: To transfer the project to the maintenance planning plant
options.D: To ensure that all data belonging to a period has been determined and is available for enterprise control

questions.explanation: It frames the period-related commercial transactions.

questions.question: What does progress analysis do?

options.A: Capitalizes costs of WBS elements and sets up provisions
options.B: Determines planned and actual project progress values and compares them
options.C: Allocates overhead through percentage-based rates
options.D: Settles costs and revenues to one or more receivers

questions.explanation: It allows corrective action if the project deviates from its plan.

questions.question: What does results analysis do?

options.A: Compares planned and actual progress values of the whole project
options.B: Adapts cost planning to changed circumstances of the project
options.C: Allocates costs between cost centers using activity types
options.D: Periodically values the project, analyzing capitalized costs of WBS elements and provisions, usually in the billing element

questions.explanation: It is usually performed in the billing element.

questions.question: How is the cost to complete in a cost forecast determined?

options.A: Actual and commitment costs already incurred plus the updated cost to complete
options.B: Planned costs minus actual costs already posted to the project
options.C: The original budget plus supplements and transfers of funds
options.D: The overhead rates multiplied by the primary cost elements

questions.explanation: The system values the remaining activities based on plan, forecast and actual values in the network.

questions.question: How does overhead costing allocate overhead?

options.A: Through settlement rules stored in the sender objects
options.B: Through activity types and the quantity of activity performed
options.C: Through percentage-based or quantity-based overhead rates, based on primary cost elements posted as overhead
options.D: Through the budget profile and the user statuses of the project

questions.explanation: Template allocation distributes overhead from business processes, cost centers or activity types.

questions.question: What does project interest calculation do?

options.A: Values fund commitments using costs, revenues or payments to achieve the best possible payment flow
options.B: Capitalizes the costs of WBS elements to fixed assets
options.C: Compares the planned and actual dates of activities
options.D: Calculates the interest on the budget of the previous year

questions.explanation: It is one of the period-end closing activities.

questions.question: Which situations produce actual costs and revenues in a project?

options.A: Only vendor invoices and customer billing
options.B: Only confirmations of network activities
options.C: Material withdrawals and goods receipts, vendor invoices, customer billing, internal activity allocations and confirmation of network activities
options.D: Only budget supplements and transfers of funds

questions.explanation: These costs are later transferred in settlement.

questions.question: To which receivers can costs and revenues of a project be settled?

options.A: Only to the cost centers of the controlling area
options.B: Only to G/L accounts in financial accounting
options.C: Only to the next project in the project hierarchy
options.D: G/L accounts in FI, fixed assets, cost accounting or profitability analysis objects, and PS objects

questions.explanation: Settlement allocates costs and revenues or results analysis data to one or more receivers.

questions.question: What do settlement rules determine?

options.A: Which WBS elements are planning elements of the project
options.B: Which portions of the sender's costs are transferred to which cost receivers
options.C: Which activities are scheduled on which work centers
options.D: Which budget profile applies to the original budget

questions.explanation: They are stored in the sender objects and contain distribution rules and settlement parameters.

questions.question: How can settlement rules be created for WBS elements?

options.A: Only by the system at the time of technical completion
options.B: Manually in the Project Builder, or with the Create Settlement Rule transaction or Fiori app using strategies
options.C: Only by copying them from a vendor master record
options.D: Only in the budget profile of the project

questions.explanation: Strategies can create rules for cost centers or profitability segments, or inherit predefined settlement rules.
